hero.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route, final flights Sept. 9
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates based on demand. JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He emphasized the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying, "It's easy. It's close." Ahern's comments reflect frustration among some passengers who valued the direct connection to New York.

While the JFK route is ending, JetBlue's Boston service from Vero Beach continues to perform well. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said the Boston route is seeing great demand, suggesting it will likely continue operating. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning in the future. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

cards.headline: World Cup final security ramped up in New Jersey with Secret Service perimeter for President Trump's attendance
cards.teaser: The World Cup final on Sunday in New Jersey will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. The final is designated a Level 1 Special Event with the highest possible security designation.
cards.body:
As Argentina and Spain prepare to take the pitch on Sunday, a sprawling network of federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies continue with a game plan two years in the making to ensure the final is safe. A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. For Sunday's match, FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says they will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there is anything that they need to do there from a threat perspective.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

cards.headline: Democratic Rep. Angie Nixon to stand trial in September for Capitol sit-in charges
cards.teaser: State Rep. Angie Nixon will face trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office.
cards.body:
Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon learned she will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Nixon and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map, which could help Republicans add up to four seats in the U.S. House. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave.

Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her campaign for U.S. Senate. The trial is scheduled after Florida's Aug. 18 primary, in which Nixon is challenging retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman for the Democratic Senate nomination. Nixon said following Wednesday's hearing that if they think the threat of a trial is going to make her back down, they picked the wrong woman.

The charges stem from the protest against the congressional redistricting plan approved by the Florida Legislature. Nixon's campaign has framed the case as an example of political retaliation for her opposition to the Republican-drawn maps.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs Blue Angels low-altitude Pensacola flyover despite safety concerns
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is encouraging low-altitude military flyovers after a Blue Angels jet flew so low over a Pensacola beach that chairs and tents went flying.
cards.body:
Video spreading widely on social media shows a jet from the Navy's demonstration squadron, the Blue Angels, flying so low over a crowded beach in Pensacola on Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears. The U.S. Navy said in a statement shortly afterward that it was conducting a thorough safety review. Then on Thursday morning, a host of Trump administration officials heaped praise on the maneuver. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote on his personal X account that the flyovers will continue until morale improves. The Pentagon's top spokesman, Sean Parnell, wrote carry on patriots on social media alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above the heads of beachgoers. The White House tweeted a cartoon showing people on a beach taking photos of a Blue Angels jet, with the words freedom and it's okay to love America.

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. His social media post was retweeted by Hegseth. Cao's post said Thursday that the Blue Angels conducted a flight debrief. Navy officials would not say if that debrief was the thorough safety review the Navy said it would conduct the day prior. Aviation safety consultant Jeff Guzzetti said a cavalier attitude like that can only lead to accidents. A Navy official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to share internal planning, said the Blue Angels' next show on Saturday will go on as scheduled.

cards.headline: Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe ordered to pay $450,000 in sexual harassment case
cards.teaser: A Leon County jury found Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation, ordering him to pay $450,000 to three plaintiffs.
cards.body:
Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe faces a $450,000 civil judgment after a Leon County jury found him liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation. The case was brought by former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother.

Basabe represented himself despite having no legal training. The trial was repeatedly interrupted by procedural mistakes and violations of the judge's orders. Circuit Judge J. Lee Marsh told Basabe, "If an attorney had done half of what you had done, they would have been sanctioned, sir." Basabe told jurors he represented himself because he wanted to demonstrate that he had nothing to hide. After the verdict, however, he acknowledged that proceeding without an attorney was a mistake.

Basabe continues to deny the underlying allegations and has not been criminally charged. An outside ethics investigation conducted for the Florida House previously reached an inconclusive finding. His political opponents quickly called for his resignation following the verdict.

Basabe is seeking reelection this fall, and the verdict could renew questions about whether House leaders will pursue disciplinary action. The judgment comes as the lawmaker campaigns for another term representing his district in the Florida Legislature.

cards.headline: Declassified report shows Chinese actor downloaded Florida voter registration data in 2022
cards.teaser: A declassified intelligence report reveals that a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter registration information from commercial websites in 2022.
cards.body:
A declassified report says a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter registration information from commercial websites in 2022. The same actor also obtained records from Colorado, Connecticut, Michigan, Oklahoma and Rhode Island. Another intelligence record lists Florida among 18 states whose voter information was obtained for possible identity matching and public-opinion analysis. The records describe the collection of voter information, some of it publicly available, but do not say Florida ballots or vote totals were altered. The 2022 report also says the actor's motive was unknown.

The White House characterized the broader collection effort as a major compromise of American voter data. However, an earlier federal assessment of the 2022 elections found no evidence that detected foreign cyber activity prevented voting, changed votes or compromised the integrity of ballots. The records were released by President Donald Trump's White House this week. Trump renewed the debate over election security during his Thursday national address, urging Congress to adopt tighter voting restrictions and repeating claims about the 2020 election that have not been substantiated. Trump did not single out Florida during his address, but records released by his White House did reference the state.

cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County jail conducted a graduation ceremony for 29 inmates who completed reentry programs designed to prepare them for life after incarceration.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County jail held a graduation ceremony Friday for 29 inmates who successfully completed reentry programs. The programs are designed to help prepare incarcerated individuals for their return to the community after serving their sentences.

The graduation ceremony marked the completion of coursework and training aimed at reducing recidivism and improving the chances of successful reintegration into society. The programs offered at the St. Lucie County jail provide inmates with skills and resources they will need upon release.

The 29 graduates participated in various reentry initiatives while incarcerated at the St. Lucie County facility. The ceremony recognized their commitment to preparing for a productive life after completing their jail terms.

cards.headline: Alex Vindman raises $8.5 million in Democratic Senate primary race
cards.teaser: Retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman raised $8.5 million during the second quarter, pushing his total receipts above $16 million in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate.
cards.body:
Retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman raised $8.5 million during the second quarter, pushing his total receipts above $16 million in the Democratic primary race for U.S. Senate. Vindman said Republicans woke up Friday morning with a bit of a panic and that the Florida Senate race is in play. He is challenging Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon for the Democratic nomination in the Aug. 18 primary.

Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million. Her campaign promoted polling showing her leading either Vindman or Nixon in a potential general-election matchup. Moody was appointed to the Senate after Marco Rubio resigned to become secretary of state. The November special election will determine who serves the final two years of Rubio's term. Nixon learned Wednesday she will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave during a protest over Florida's newly approved congressional map.

cards.headline: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback faces residency challenge in court
cards.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback will defend his eligibility to remain in the primary next week as an opponent challenges whether he meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement.
cards.body:
Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback will defend his eligibility to remain in the primary next week as Lt. Jay Collins, one of his opponents, challenges whether he meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governor. Collins argues that records showing Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., mean he does not satisfy the requirement. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida and maintained the state as his permanent home.

A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin Tuesday in Tallahassee. Because primary ballots have already been printed, the judge has said a ruling against Fishback could require election officials to post notices and decline to count votes cast for him.

hero.headline: Lionel Messi photographed bathing Lamine Yamal as baby nearly two decades before World Cup final matchup
hero.teaser: A Barcelona photographer captured images of teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in 2007 for a charity calendar. The two players will now face each other in Sunday's World Cup final when Argentina plays Spain.
hero.body:
Almost two decades ago, photographer Joan Monfort took photos of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing a cute baby boy in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. That infant was Lamine Yamal. Now those images of the longhaired Messi, his hands covered in soap suds, have become the most talked about in the runup to Sunday's World Cup final, when Messi's Argentina will play Yamal's Spain. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for the Associated Press from his home in Barcelona, said he has never been a believer or thought that anything was destined to occur, but he is beginning to have his doubts. Luck dictated that Yamal's mother, who appears in the calendar photo, won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate in the 2007 photo shoot. A tearful Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later. The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior.

Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal was enjoying his international breakout and led Spain to the title. Monfort, 58, said interest in his photos has skyrocketed and that this has exploded all over the world. He is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey. Monfort said his heart is split and he does not know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win, as he has an everlasting love for the best player of all time but Yamal has broken the mold and represents a new, diverse Spain thanks to his parents from Morocco and Equatorial Guinea.

cards.headline: Argentina defeats England 2-1 with late rally to advance to World Cup final
cards.teaser: Argentina scored two goals in the final minutes to overcome England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinals on Wednesday. The defending champions will face Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
cards.body:
Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute, Argentina rallied for a 2-1 victory over England on Wednesday with goals from Enzo Fernandez and substitute Lautaro Martinez. At the final whistle, Lionel Messi fell to his knees in celebration while England players collapsed in disbelief. Argentina will take on European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves while Mac Allister sent a header off the post as wave after wave of Argentina attacks came. Messi fed the ball to Fernandez to sweep in the equalizer from outside the box in the 85th minute. Two minutes into stoppage time, Messi sent in a cross for Martinez to head in the winner.

Lautaro Martinez said he dreamed it and told Alexis Mac Allister that he was going to score. England captain Harry Kane said he was gutted for the team, the staff, and the fans, and that to fall short like they did is just gutting. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team proved themselves and were ready to try to win, adding that they are unique and its not arrogance, its from the heart.

cards.headline: Major League Baseball restricts dugout iPad use to prevent AI from making in-game decisions
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night. MLB said the tabs had expanded iPad use beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions and pitch calling.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started. Morgan Sword, MLB executive vice president of baseball operations, wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts from Treasure Coast earn top 15 national finish, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.body:
Three young gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer competed as one unit on the national stage last month, each having found their way to the sport through different paths. Skylar Rose-Daris said it wasn't really gymnastics that drew her in, but rather the fact that she knew how to do a cartwheel. Victoria Supan was inspired by all the gymnasts she saw on YouTube and how amazing they are and how fun it looks. Charli Rine said she loves gymnastics because she learns new things. The trio competed locally, traveled, and advanced to states and regionals during what Head Coach Candice Lazuka described as a really good season.

At AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee, the gymnasts secured a top 15 finish and came close to a perfect score. Lazuka said it is hard to get a perfect 10, but the team got a 9.9 and were very close to a 10. The finish qualified the team for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Rose-Daris said it is going to be really fun that she is going to an entire different part of the world. Supan said it is happy and exciting at the same time. Rine has a specific goal heading into the competition, saying she is focused on getting first place on floors.

cards.teaser: Alexandra Belcher, a 34-year-old Florida beachgoer, called the Blue Angels flyover a once-in-a-lifetime experience despite the unusual proximity of the aircraft.
cards.body:
Florida beachgoer Alexandra Belcher, 34, called the Blue Angels flyover this week a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Belcher said she did not realize how close it was until everyone around her said that was so cool. She said it was not normal but was a blessing to be able to witness that with everybody that she was with. Video spreading widely on social media shows a jet from the Navy's demonstration squadron flying so low over a crowded beach in Pensacola on Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears.

Former Transportation Department Inspector General Mary Schiavo said these flyovers probably do not violate military rules because the Pentagon does not have the same restrictions on flying low over people that the FAA imposes on civilian flights. Schiavo, who is also a pilot and used to work in air shows years ago, said the Blue Angels are air demonstration teams and what they do is exceedingly dangerous, amazing and wonderful, but dangerous. A Navy official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to share internal planning, said the Blue Angels' next show on Saturday will go on as scheduled.

hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
hero.teaser: Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall, and the gap between what the county needs and what it can afford could shape how residents get around for decades.
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next 20 years, a gap that could determine how residents travel for decades to come.

The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. That means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Nearly all of the available funding comes from state and federal sources, with only $10 million coming from local revenue. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. Without funding for these widening projects, the county will be unable to address growing congestion on these corridors.

State Road 710 stands out as among the county's highest priorities and has been the subject of repeated safety concerns. About $300 million in projects are planned for the corridor, reflecting the urgent need for improvements on this route. The massive funding shortfall highlights the challenge facing Martin County as it tries to balance transportation demands with limited financial resources over the coming decades.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce woman wins $5 million on $20 Florida Lottery scratch-off ticket
hero.body:
Maria Duran, 57, of St. Lucie County claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6, Florida Lottery officials announced Friday. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138.

Duran purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The $20 scratch-off game offers overall odds of winning at 1-in-2.90.

The chance of winning the $5 million top prize playing this game is 1-in-4,018,135, according to lottery officials. The $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH game is one of several high-value scratch-off games offered by the Florida Lottery.

The Fort Pierce convenience store that sold the winning ticket will receive a bonus commission for selling the jackpot-winning scratch-off. Duran's win was one of several lottery jackpots claimed by Florida players this week.

hero.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to New York JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He explained that JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said. Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He noted the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said.

The Boston route from Vero Beach is performing well, according to Dambeck. "Boston is seeing great demand," Dambeck said. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning in the future. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.
